points.description: States the purpose: to achieve a more efficient broadcast than flooding, i.e. to minimize the number of duplicate packets in the network when broadcasting.

Reverse Path Forwarding: on receiving a packet from sender S via neighbor N, the node checks its unicast routing table and forwards the packet to all adjacent nodes (except N) only if it would itself send packets to S via N (i.e. the packet arrived on the best route); otherwise it discards it.

Reverse Path Broadcast: nodes monitor unicast traffic to learn which spanning trees (shortest paths between node pairs) they are part of. It works like Reverse Path Forwarding, except it forwards packets only on lines that are part of a spanning tree (excluding the line to N).

rubric.notes: Full marks need the purpose (fewer duplicates than flooding), the RPF check against the unicast routing table, and RPB's restriction to spanning-tree lines learned from unicast traffic. Equivalent wording is accepted. Award marks only for the ideas present.
